# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *Wuthering Heights* that had been on the shelf since the Clinton administration. Marisol Reyes found it while shelving returns: a faint pencil mark beside a passage describing the moors, and in the margin, in small, precise handwriting, *"Heathcliff would not have said this. Too self-aware."*

She almost missed it. The mark was that light, that careful—as if the writer wanted to be noticed only by someone reading closely. Marisol held the book under the circulation desk lamp and frowned. Pencil, not pen. Erasable. Almost polite, as vandalism went.

She should have erased it. That was policy. Instead, she flipped through the rest of the novel and found two more notes, both in the same hand. One corrected a date. The other simply said, *"Yes."*

The Seaview Public Library sat three blocks from the harbor in the town of Kestrel Point, where the fog came in most evenings like a tide of its own.
